messages.title: Messages

stories.emptyDesc: Stories are captured in real-time when posted, and from WhatsApp's history sync on connect. Only stories posted while the tracker is active and connected can be saved.

qr.instruction: Open WhatsApp on your phone → Linked devices → Link a device.

phone.instruction: Enter your phone in international format (e.g. +14155551234). Then in WhatsApp: Linked devices → Link a device → Link with phone number instead.
phone.enterCode: Enter this code on your phone:

stats.activitySummaryTooltip: A quick snapshot of this contact's WhatsApp activity in the selected time range. Use the range tabs to compare behavior across different periods — for example, whether they're more active this week than last.
stats.onlineTimeTooltip: High online time doesn't mean they saw your messages — they may be active in other chats. But it shows they are available and using WhatsApp, making it a good window to reach out.
stats.picChangesTooltip: Even a single change is notable — it may signal a mood shift, a new relationship, or a seasonal update. Each picture is saved and viewable in the Presence tab with its timestamp.
stats.aboutChangesTooltip: Frequent About changes can reveal someone actively curating their self-presentation. Each change is logged with the full text and timestamp, visible in the Presence tab's Status History.
stats.chartTooltip: Spikes on specific days can be correlated with events or conversations. Days with zero minutes may mean they switched to another device, had a connectivity issue, or were offline intentionally.
stats.chartDesc: Daily breakdown of online time across the selected period

presence.sectionTooltip: These metrics are computed from WhatsApp presence events — when the contact appeared online or went offline. Accuracy depends on how long tracking has been active and whether WhatsApp presence visibility is enabled for this contact.
presence.sectionDesc: Online activity summary based on tracked presence events.
presence.avgSessionDesc: Average duration of a single online session.
presence.avgSessionTooltip: Short sessions (<3 min) suggest quick message checks; longer sessions mean active browsing. Combined with peak hours, this reveals their daily phone habits.
presence.longestSessionTooltip: An unusually long session may indicate a video call, a busy work period, or a day spent on the phone. Compare it to the average to see how typical it was.
presence.dailyAvgDesc: Average online time per day. ▲▼ = change vs. prior week.
presence.dailyAvgTooltip: Compare this to your own online time to gauge whether you're both active at similar intensities. A rising trend means they've been using WhatsApp more recently.
presence.onlineStreakTooltip: A long active streak means they use WhatsApp consistently every day. Useful for knowing they're reliably reachable.
presence.offlineForTooltip: They haven't appeared online since this time. This could mean the app is closed, presence is hidden, or they are inactive.
presence.longestOfflineDesc: Longest gap between any two active days.
presence.longestOfflineTooltip: A long offline streak may mark a trip, illness, or a period off WhatsApp entirely. Comparing it to the tracking period shows whether this was unusual or routine.
presence.nightOwlDesc: Share of online time between midnight and 5am.
presence.nightOwlTooltip: A high score (>20%) suggests late-night habits, shift work, or a different time zone. This is the best time to reach them if you want a faster reply late at night.
presence.consistencyDesc: How predictable their online schedule is.
presence.consistencyTooltip: High consistency (>70) means their schedule is very regular — you can reliably reach them at the same times each day. Low consistency (below 30) means their WhatsApp usage is sporadic and hard to predict.
presence.picChangesDesc: Average days between profile picture changes.
presence.picChangesTooltip: Frequent changes (every few days) signal someone socially active or going through life changes. Rare changes (>90 days) suggest a stable or more private persona.
presence.peakHoursTooltip: The best window to send a message and get a timely reply. If their peak hours don't overlap with yours, expect longer response gaps even when they're active.
presence.peakHoursDesc: Hours with activity above 50% of their peak
presence.sleepWindowTooltip: Knowing their estimated sleep window helps you avoid sending messages at inappropriate hours and better understand their daily rhythm. Requires at least 3 recurring overnight offline gaps (≥3h, starting 8pm–4am) to compute.
presence.sleepWindowDesc: Estimated from recurring overnight offline gaps
presence.trackingPeriodTooltip: Longer tracking periods produce more accurate patterns — at least 2 weeks is needed for reliable daily averages, and 4+ weeks for streak and sleep estimates. Short periods may not reflect long-term behavior.
presence.trackingPeriodDesc: Date range of recorded presence events
presence.peakHoursChartTooltip: If their peak hours don't overlap with yours, most messages will sit unread for hours before a reply — which can feel like low engagement even when they're active. Use this to find the best time to reach them.
presence.peakHoursChartDesc: Total online minutes per hour of the day across all tracked days
presence.mostActiveDaysTooltip: Weekend vs. weekday peaks reveal the nature of their WhatsApp usage. High weekend activity often signals personal, social use. High weekday activity may indicate professional use or habit. Weekends are shown in a different color.
presence.mostActiveDaysDesc: Total online minutes per day of the week (weekends highlighted)
presence.heatmapTooltip: Clusters of dark cells reveal sustained active periods. Gaps (light or empty weeks) can mark vacations, illness, or extended time off WhatsApp. Each cell is one day — darker green = more total online time.
presence.heatmapDesc: Daily online time over the last 16 weeks — darker = more active
presence.trend30Tooltip: An upward trend means they've been more active on WhatsApp recently. A downward trend may mean they're busier, switched devices, or are spending less time on their phone. Sudden spikes often correspond to specific events.
presence.trend30Desc: Online minutes per day over the last 30 days

timeline.title: Timeline
timeline.description: When you first and last exchanged messages, how many days had at least one message, and your longest streak of consecutive active days.
timeline.tooltip: Streak length and active-day density reveal the texture of the relationship. A long span with low active-day % means contact is rare and scattered. A long streak that ended months ago may mark when things changed.
timeline.longestStreakDesc: Consecutive days with at least one message.
timeline.longestStreakTooltip: Long streaks signal periods of daily, sustained connection. A streak that ended long ago may mark when the relationship shifted — worth comparing to Monthly Evolution.

initiation.title: Initiation & Response
initiation.description: A session starts when either side breaks 3+ hours of silence. Shows who starts conversations and how quickly each side replies.
initiation.tooltip: When one person initiates 70%+ of sessions, the other may be less invested or waiting to be reached. Reply time gaps between 'you' and 'them' reveal asymmetry in attention — a large difference often indicates who values the conversation more.
initiation.longestSilenceDesc: Longest gap between any two messages.
initiation.longestSilenceTooltip: An unusually long single silence may mark a conflict, a trip, or a cooling point in the relationship. Compare it to average silence to see if it was a one-off or the norm.
initiation.avgSilenceTooltip: High average silence (>12h) means this is an asynchronous relationship — messages are read and replied to later, not in real-time. Low silence (<30min) means both sides are typically active at the same time.

volume.title: Volume
volume.description: Total messages, words, and media sent by each side. The bar shows your share of total messages.
volume.tooltip: A persistent imbalance (one person above 65%) suggests who drives the conversation. Word balance often tells more than message count — short frequent replies look very different from long infrequent ones.

hourly.title: Messages by hour
hourly.description: How many messages each person sends per hour of the day. Blue = you, gray = them.
hourly.tooltip: Overlapping peaks mean you communicate in real-time. If your high-activity hours don't align, most messages sit unread for hours before a reply — which inflates response times and can feel one-sided.

weekday.title: Messages by weekday
weekday.description: Total messages per day of the week. Blue = you, gray = them.
weekday.tooltip: Weekend vs. weekday peaks reveal the nature of the relationship. Both sides active on weekends often signals a personal bond rather than a professional or obligatory one.

temporal.title: Temporal patterns
temporal.description: Percentage of messages sent between midnight and 5am by each side.
temporal.tooltip: High night-message rates (>15%) suggest conversations happen when the person is most relaxed and unguarded, or indicate very different time zones. It can also signal emotional intensity — late-night messaging is rarely casual.

emotion.title: Emotion fingerprint
emotion.description: Messages classified by emotional tone using keyword patterns. Bars show your share vs theirs for each emotion.
emotion.tooltip: The balance of emotions reveals who brings positivity, who asks for support, and the overall register of the relationship. Gratitude or encouragement heavily skewed to one side can signal a support asymmetry — one person giving more than they receive.

language.title: Language fingerprint
language.description: Most frequently used emojis, words (stop-words removed), and web domains from shared links — ranked by count for each side.
language.tooltip: Shared vocabulary and overlapping emojis signal linguistic rapport and mirroring — a subtle sign of closeness. Domains reveal what content you exchange: news, videos, social media. Wildly different word lists may mean the conversation stays shallow.

monthly.title: Monthly evolution
monthly.description: Month-by-month message counts. The last 3 months are bold to highlight recent activity.
monthly.tooltip: Rising or falling totals show whether the relationship is growing, stable, or cooling. A sudden drop in a previously active month often corresponds to a life event, conflict, or natural drift — cross-reference with the timeline.

indicators.title: Indicators
indicators.description: Aggregate metrics summarizing the overall balance and dynamics of the conversation.
indicators.tooltip: Look for imbalances across all indicators together: if your message balance, word balance, and initiation % are all above 60%, you are carrying the relationship — the other person is mostly responding rather than reaching out.
indicators.msgBalanceDesc: Your share of total messages sent.
indicators.msgBalanceTooltip: Healthy conversations sit between 40–60%. A persistent number above 65% means you are sending most of the messages and likely driving the conversation.
indicators.wordBalanceDesc: Your share of total words written.
indicators.wordBalanceTooltip: Compare this to your message balance. If your word % is much higher than your message %, your messages are longer — you may be explaining, elaborating, or carrying more emotional weight.
indicators.activeDaysPctDesc: Days with at least one message, out of the total span.
indicators.activeDaysPctTooltip: Below 20% with a long span means contact is rare and spread out. Above 70% means you're in near-daily contact. This is one of the strongest signals of how central someone is to your daily life.
indicators.medianReplyDesc: Median response time across both sides.
indicators.medianReplyTooltip: The median is more reliable than the average because it isn't skewed by a few very long gaps. A short median means the conversation flows quickly; a long one means messages often go unanswered for hours.
indicators.initiationYouDesc: How often you start a new conversation session.
indicators.initiationYouTooltip: If you're consistently above 70%, you are the one keeping this relationship alive. If you're below 30%, they reach out far more often. Neither is inherently bad — but a mismatch is worth noticing.
indicators.syncLaughDaysDesc: Days when both sides sent laughter messages.
indicators.syncLaughDaysTooltip: A day where both of you laughed in the same conversation is a proxy for genuine mutual enjoyment. More sync laugh days generally mean more comfort and shared humor in the relationship.
indicators.shareTrendDesc: Change in your message share over recent months.
indicators.shareTrendTooltip: A rising trend means you're sending a growing share of messages lately. A falling trend means the other person is becoming more active, or you are becoming less so — either way, the dynamic is shifting.
